short: Sensor, murmur mode and HMM retraining (M05, M04, M03) repeat the group's 2003 design and results; noise robustness lacks noise levels and an air-microphone baseline.
position: The paper [@nakajima2006nam] changes the sensor (M05), the speaking mode (M04) and the acoustic-model transfer (M03), and all three are standard: they are the design of the group's 2003 reports [@nakajima2003icassp; @heracleous2003accurate], whose environment A-C results Table 1 repeats to rounding despite a larger described training set (§3.5), and whispered 20,000-word dictation existed in 2002 [@tatara2002experiments]. The noise-robustness claim (§3.6, §4) rests on unmeasured noise and no air-microphone baseline; a close-talking microphone held 91.7-91.9% in the group's [concurrent] TV and music conditions [@heracleous2004audible], and live noise at 60 dBA later cut NAM accuracy to 53.3% [@heracleous2007unvoiced]. The 93.3% quiet result is one speaker, speaker-dependent, with test text of unstated overlap with training.
